title: Finite Q3 complex OS transfer-word Gram perturbation
question: Can the R340 Complex Gram perturbation inequality be instantiated on actual finite Q3 Euclidean transfer-word matrices, while keeping common-carrier and thermodynamic uniformity hypotheses open?

exact_statement.complex_gram_entry: G_f(i,j)=sum_k conjugate(f(i,k)) f(j,k) for finite complex vectors.
exact_statement.decomposition: conjugate(f_i) f_j-conjugate(g_i) g_j = conjugate(f_i-g_i) f_j + conjugate(g_i)(f_j-g_j).
exact_statement.q3_vectorization: Each finite energy-basis transfer-word matrix F is flattened into a complex Hilbert-Schmidt vector; the finite Gram entry is sum conjugate(F_i)F_j divided by the positive partition function.

model.comparison: f uses tau_pair_fractions[0] and g uses tau_pair_fractions[1] for the same graph, source and observable kinds
model.observables: A_x=exp(i a q_x/hbar), B_x=exp(i a p_x/hbar)

adversarial_review.check: The Gram uses conjugation on the first vector and the two-term decomposition keeps that orientation; no real-only substitution is made.
Each F matrix is flattened only within one declared finite graph and energy basis; no cross-volume identification is assumed.
The raw R340 inequality is applied before division by the positive finite partition function, so normalization cannot reverse the inequality.
Identity and inequality residuals use manifest absolute and relative tolerances; no floating value is promoted as an exact physical constant.
All finite source sites in bond2, square4 and grid2x3 are recomputed, but this finite coverage is not source-uniform thermodynamic control.
A positive Hamiltonian-observable commutator witness is retained for each graph; the transfer words are not treated as commuting factors.
The independent lane rebuilds tensor operators, Q3 Hamiltonian, spectra, transfer matrices and complex sums without importing the primary lane.
Finite complex vector instantiation does not close a common OS carrier, exhaustion Cauchy estimate, common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A.

lean_crosscheck.role: R340 is the exact Complex Hilbert-space perturbation bridge; Python instantiates it on finite Q3 transfer-word matrices, while all common-carrier and limit assumptions remain explicit.

qft_interface.closed: For the declared finite Q3 graphs, sources, beta values and two tau contexts, the actual energy-basis transfer-word matrices are finite complex Hilbert-Schmidt vectors and satisfy the R340 Gram perturbation bound within recorded numerical tolerances.
qft_interface.open: No cross-volume common Hilbert carrier, source/volume/cutoff/beta-uniform vector estimate, exhaustion Cauchy theorem, direct D/delta-D convergence, common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A follows.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary finite QFT interface only; no physical reference, heat_root_incidence, canonical A1/R-192 production owner, Sector-A closure or Pre-A closure is supplied.

next_action: Use the explicit finite vector-difference terms as the input contract for a cross-volume common-carrier test. Supply an actual isometric transport or a uniform source/volume/cutoff/beta bound; if neither exists, record the missing-interface obstruction rather than promoting finite Gram control.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite Complex transfer-word instantiation. It is not a thermodynamic OS reconstruction, common-alpha theorem, mass-gap proof, continuum result, or Clay result.
no_overclaim: This package proves only the finite Complex Gram perturbation theorem and its numerical instantiation on the declared Q3 matrices. It does not prove a common OS Hilbert space, thermodynamic dynamics, common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, GNS mass gap, continuum removal, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or a Clay result.
